newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia trade deficit to decline sharply - govt.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia trade deficit to decline sharply - govt.

text.p: Malaysia's trade deficit will decline sharply to 340 million ringgit in 1997 from 5.2 billion in 1996, the Finance Ministry said in its annual Economic Report released on Friday.
Malaysia posted a 9.35 billion ringgit deficit in 1995.

Total exports (fob) are projected to increase by 9.4 percent in 1997 to 210.65 billion in 1997 after rising 4.1 percent to 192.60 billion in 1996 and 20.2 percent to 184.48 billion in 1995, the report said.
Total imports (cif) are projected to increase to 210.99 billion ringgit in 1997 from 197.80 billion in 1996 and 194.34 billion in 1995, it said.
Malaysia recorded a trade deficit of 1.4 billion ringgit in the first seven months of 1996 compared with a 6.9 billion ringgit deficit in the corresponding period last year.
The expected lower deficit in 1996 results from modest export growth, a 6.9 percent decrease in imported capital goods and a small increase in imported consumer items, the report said.

The merchandise account, which does not include freight and insurance charges, will post a surplus of 4.6 billion ringgit in 1996 against a 200 million ringgit surplus last year due to a significant decrease in imports, the report said.
The lower import growth mainly reflects fewer aircraft and ships purchased by airlines and shipping firms, it said.
The report said imports of intermediate goods are expected to grow at a slower rate of 3.8 percent in 1996 to 131.1 billion ringgit against an increase of 27.7 percent in 1995.
Manufactured exports remain the largest contributor to total exports, rising 14.9 percent in the first seven months of the year and accounting for 81 percent of total exports.
Electronic and electrical products continued to constitute the largest share of manufactured exports, accounting for 66 percent during the period.
For the whole of 1996, exports of manufactured goods are expected to record a moderate growth of 5.8 percent after registering a 22.9 percent growth in 1995, the report said.
But the ministry said export growth faces trouble ahead.

Malaysia is due to "graduate" from the U.S. Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) programme on January 1, 1997 and the European Union is also expected to cut preferential tariffs for Malaysia under its GSP. Thus, Malaysia may lose its competitive edge to other GSP beneficiaries such as China, Philippines, Thailand and Indonesia, the report said.
